assumptions: The edge assumes piSignage and RaspAP are co-located or share a filesystem so the piSignage file-read primitive can reach RaspAP files.
The edge assumes RaspAP configuration or session files contain a reusable admin credential or session token.
The edge assumes any extracted credential/session remains valid for RaspAP 2.5 and grants access to includes/webconsole.php.

evidence_quotes.quote: piSignage Arbitrary File Read via Path Traversal (CVE-2021-34336)
RaspAP Authenticated Remote Command Execution via Web Console (CVE-2021-33357)

missing_conditions: same-host or shared-filesystem deployment of piSignage and RaspAP
specific RaspAP configuration/session file paths readable via the path traversal
presence of admin credentials or a valid session token in those files
validity of leaked credentials/session for RaspAP 2.5 authentication
network reachability of the RaspAP web interface and includes/webconsole.php
source-side low-privilege authenticated access to piSignage player API, if required by the source precondition
response.reason: The source CVE-2021-34336 is described as piSignage arbitrary file read via path traversal, so its bounded effect is unauthorized file disclosure on the Raspberry Pi filesystem. The target CVE-2021-33357 requires authenticated access to the RaspAP 2.5 web interface before web-console command execution. The edge claim bridges these by asserting that the source path traversal can extract RaspAP configuration files and admin session/credentials and thereby gain authenticated access to includes/webconsole.php. That bridge is overreaching: no supplied description or environment observation confirms same-host deployment, readability of RaspAP-specific files, presence/validity of reusable credentials or sessions, or target authentication. The edge is only potentially plausible under those unverified conditions and should not enter a strict graph as stated.
